UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.
This Miscellaneous Application is at the instance of the National Highways Authority of India.

2. In the Miscellaneous Application, the National Highway Authority of India has prayed for the following reliefs:-
a) Allow the application and pass an appropriate Clarification/Direction in the order dated 23.09.2022 in Miscellaneous application No. 1172/2021 in Civil Appeal No.
10501/2017 to the extent of applicability of First Schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ('2013 Act') in terms of the said order.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: b) Pass any such order(s) as this Hon'ble Court, may deem fit and proper under the circumstances of the case.

3. We heard Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, the learned ASG appearing for the applicant and Mr. Kailash J.
Kashyap, the learned counsel appearing for the original-appellants namely Sanwarmal Singhaniya Memorial Trust & Anr.
4.

We take notice of the order passed by this Court dated 28.11.2019 in Civil Appeal No. 10501/2017 which was filed by the Trust against the judgment passed by the Rajasthan High Court under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

The order reads thus:-
The present appeal is filed against a judgment dated 30.06.2016 of the Rajasthan High Court in which, under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996,
Sanwarmal Singhaniya Memorial Trust vs National Highways Authority Of India on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191291336/
2 the Court has set aside the Arbitration Award as well as the order of the learned Additional District Judge dismissing the Section 34 application therefrom.

sentences.text:
In the present case, a Notification under Section 3A of the National Highways Act,
1956, was issued on 05.03.2013 taking over 40,000 odd square meters of land.
The claim that was made by the appellant in this case was for a sum of Rs.56.60 crores.
However, by an Award dated 10.02.2014 passed by the competent Authority, a sum of Rs.29.8 crores was awarded as compensation.

Being dissatisfied, both the parties went to the learned Arbitrator, who gave his Award dated 13.04.2015, in which the selfsame amount of R5.29.80 crores was awarded as compensation, relying upon the District Level Committee's rates in order to determine the market value.
A section 34 petition filed by the respondent was dismissed on 07.04.2016.

Against this, an appeal was filed by the respondent which was allowed by the impugned Judgment in which, relying upon the Judgment of this Court in Jawajee Nagnatham v. Revenue Divisional Officer Adilabad A.P. and Ors. [1994(4) SCC 595], the High court held that fixation of market Value could not be merely on the basis of the District level Committee's rates, even though no such objection has been raised by the appellant.

entities.text: Jawajee Nagnatham v. Revenue Divisional Officer Adilabad A.P. and Ors. [1994(4) SCC 595]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This being the case, the learned Single Judge set aside the Section 34 Judgment and the Arbitration Award and referred the case back to the competent Authority to fix Market Value in accordance with law.
Having heard learned counsel for both the parties, we are of the view that the learned Single Judge ought not to have interfered with the Addl. District Judge's judgement.

First and foremost, our judgment which was referred to and relied upon, was a case in which this Court specifically stated that the Basic Valuation Register prepared and maintained for the purpose of collecting Stamp Duty in that case, had no statutory base or force and could not therefore be relied upon.

In the present case, it has correctly been pointed out to us that the District Level Committee's rates are by a Committee which consists of the District Collector, the Additional District Magistrate and the Sub- Registrar, all of whom fix Market Value under Rule 58 of the Rajasthan Stamp Rules, 2004, thereby giving a statutory flavour to the Market Value fixed.
This being the case, we set aside the judgment of the learned single Judge and restore that of the learned Additional District Judge dated 07.04.2016.
AS per our order in Union of India & Anr. v. Tarsem Singh & Ors.

entities.text: Union of India & Anr. v. Tarsem Singh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , statutory benefits that are available under the Land Acquisition Act will be given in addition.
The appeal is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
5. Later, the Trust came back to this Court with the miscellaneous application seeking appropriate clarification in the matter.
Such application filed by the Trust came to be disposed of vide the order dated 23.9.2022.

The order reads thus:-

sentences.text: On 28th November 2019, this Court had allowed the appeal of the landowners in connection with the claim arising out of acquisition of their land under the National Highways Act, 1956 (the 1956 Act).
The dispute pertaining to quantum of compensation had gone for arbitration from which the appeal arose.
But in this order, we are not referring to the history of the proceedings resulting in filing of the present application.
This application is essentially for clarification of a part of the order passed by this Court on 28th November 2019, allowing the appeal of the landowners.

In this order,
it was, inter-alia, directed:-
....This being the case, we set aside the judgment of the learned Single Judge and restore that of the learned Additional District Judge dated 07.04.2016.
As per our order in Union of India & Anr. v. Tarsem Singh &. Ors. [2019 (12) SCALE 648], statutory benefits that are available under the Land Acquisition Act will be given in addition.

entities.text: Union of India & Anr. v. Tarsem Singh &. Ors. [2019 (12) SCALE 648]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appeal is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
So far as the aforesaid order is concerned
, a review petition filed by the NHAI was dismissed.

The only clarification sought by the landowners in this application is as to whether the words, statutory benefits that are available under the Land Acquisition Act appearing in the penultimate paragraph extracted above, would mean the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: An application registered as I.A. No.141352, was filed in connection with the main appeal by the applicant landowners.
This application was for bringing on records additional documents.

One of the documents referred to in this application contains a memorandum issued by the Government of India on 28th December, 2017 (No.
NHAI- 11011/30/2015-LA) captioned Land Acquisition under the National Highways Act, 1956-comprehensive guidelines thereon.
Certain provisions of the 2013 Act have been made applicable to the proceedings under the 1956 Act with effect from 1st January 2015 as per the said guidelines.

Clause 4.6 (iii) of the said guidelines dated 28.12.2017 stipulates:-
(iii) By now, it is also a settled proposition that the First, Second and Third Schedule of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 shall be applicable to the NH Act, 1956 with effect from 01.01.2015.

As such, the following is clarified:
(a) All cases of Land acquisition where the Awards had not been announced under Section 3G of the NH Act till 31.12.2014 or where such awards had been announced Sanwarmal Singhaniya Memorial Trust vs National Highways Authority Of India on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191291336/
4 but compensation had not been paid in respect of majority of the land holdings under acquisition as on 31.12.2014, the compensation would be payable in accordance with the First Schedule of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.

entities.text: Sanwarmal Singhaniya Memorial Trust vs National Highways Authority Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (b) In cases, where the land acquisition process was initiated and award of compensation under Section 3G had also been announced before 01.01.2015 but the full amount of Award had not been deposited by the acquiring agency with the CALA, the compensation amount would be liable to be determined in accordance with the First Schedule w.e.f. 01.01.2015;

(c) In cases, where the process of acquisition of land stood completed (i.e. Award under Section 3G announced by CALA, amount deposited by the acquiring agency with the CALA, and compensation paid to the landowners in respect of majority of the land under acquisition) as on or before 31.12.2014, the process would be deemed to have been completed and settled.
Such cases would not be re-
opened.
In the present case, date of the award is 10.02.2014 and the date of deposit of full amount of award is 26.11.2015.
This has been stated in a tabular statement made in paragraph 2 of the reply affidavit of the respondent to the present application (i.e., M.A. No.1172 of 2021).
Reference to Land Acquisition Act in the order also includes in it the provisions of the First Schedule to the 2013 Act.
The case of Tarsem Singh dealt with, inter-alia, constitutional validity of Section 3J of the 1956 Act.

In this judgment, it was, inter-alia, held by a Coordinate Bench of this Court:-
52.

There is no doubt that the learned Solicitor General, in the aforesaid two orders,
has conceded the issue raised in these cases.

This assumes importance in view of the plea of Shri Divan that the impugned judgments should be set aside on the ground that when the arbitral awards did not provide for solatium or interest, no Section 34 petition having been filed by the landowners on this score, the Division Bench judgments that are impugned before us ought not to have allowed solatium and/or interest.

Ordinarily, we would have acceded to this plea, but given the fact that the Government itself is of the view that solatium and interest should be granted even in cases that arise between 1997 and 2015, in the interest of justice we decline to interfere with such orders, given our discretionary jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.

We therefore declare that the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act relating to solatium and interest contained in Sections 23(1-A) and (2) and interest payable in terms of Section 28 proviso will apply to acquisitions made under the National Highways Act.

Consequently, the provision of Section 3-J is, to this extent, violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and, therefore,
declared to be unconstitutional.
Accordingly, appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 9599 of 2019 is dismissed.
On behalf of the respondent(s), applicability of the said guidelines has not been disputed.

It is, however, submitted by the learned Additional Solicitor General that a large number of landowners had been given compensation in terms of Section 3G of the 1956 Act before the stipulated date and as such the case of the applicant(s) ought not to come within sub-clause (a) of the said guidelines.

Mr.
Sibal, however, points out that Clause (b) thereof is applicable in the case of the appellants/applicants.

The three sub-clauses of para 4.6(iii) contemplate different situations and context under which the First Schedule of the 2013 Act would be Sanwarmal Singhaniya Memorial Trust vs National Highways Authority Of India on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191291336/
5 applicable and the context in which the cases would not be reopened.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The guidelines formed part of the cause papers of the appeal proceedings and a plain reading of the said guidelines reveals that it was not intended that the payment of compensation as per the first schedule to the 2013 Act should be made on compliance of the conditions prescribed in all the three sub clauses of clause 4.6(iii) of the said guidelines cumulatively.

So far as the present applicant(s) are concerned, their position fits into aforesaid sub-clause (b) and hence we clarify the order passed on 28.11.2019 to the extent that the sub-clause 4.6 (iii)(b) of the a f o r e s a i d g u i d e l i n e s d a t e d 2 8 t h D e c e m b e r 2 0 1 7 w o u l d b e a p p l i c a b l e t o t h e applicant(s)/petitioner(s).
Accordingly, I.A. No. 87069/2021 and the miscellaneous application stands disposed of along with pending application(s), if any.
There shall be no order as to costs.
6. We are of the view that there was no good reason for the applicant to come before us with the present application and seek further clarification.
Whatever had to be clarified has been very lucidly clarified by this Court vide the order dated 23.9.2022 referred to above.

The parties shall abide by the order passed by this Court dated 23.9.2022.
7.
With the aforesaid, this Miscellaneous Application stands disposed of.

(CHANDRESH) (POOJA SHARMA)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS COURT MASTER (NSH)
